newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rabobank sees modest Dutch rate rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank sees modest Dutch rate rise in 1997.

text.p: Cooperative bank Rabobank said on Tuesday it expected Dutch money market rates and long-term interest rates to show a modest rise in 1997.
Rabobank said in its "Vision on 1997" report that Dutch three-month interest rates could rise to 3.25-3.50 percent in 1997 from 3.00 percent, currently.
"Dutch long-term interest rates are expected to rise to 6.00 or 6.25 percent at the start of 1997, but will slip again later," it said in the report.
Rabobank said long-term interest rates were likely to come down to between 5.75 and 6.00 percent later in 1997, which would be a little higher than the current 5.72-percent yield for ten-year bonds.
It said the market would closely watch the German and U.S. markets for the direction of long-term rates.
Rabobank added the rise in money market rates would be triggered by the recovery in the German economy, which would underline the perception that the period of interest rates cuts had come to a halt.
It said the Dutch guilder was likely to keep steady versus the German mark in 1997, but the gap between Dutch money rates and their German equivalent was seen narrowing.
The Dutch guilder was at 112.17 per 100 marks in mid-afternoon, weaker than the 111.965 quote at the start of 1996.

Rabobank said in its report the gap for the Dutch and German three-month AIBOR-tariff widened to 67 basis points last May, but this narrowed to a more stable level later as the Dutch three-month AIBOR was only 25 basis points below the German equivalent.
"As result of the continuing strength of the guilder, we foresee Dutch three-month rates will remain (about ten basis points) below the German rate," it said.
